description: One zombie on Earth. SZR model with latency of Alemi, Bierbaum, Myers, Sethna, 'You Can Run, You Can Hide: The Epidemiology and Statistical Mechanics of Zombies', Phys. Rev. E 92, 052801 (2015), arXiv:1503.01104, on a world grid of 0.25 degrees (GHS-POP 2025 population), plus air travel of bitten people (OpenFlights routes).
source_parameters: Table 1 of the paper: beta 3.6e-3 /hr/person for 3 km cells, alpha = kappa/beta = 0.8 (Witkowski & Blais fit to Night of the Living Dead and Shaun of the Dead), eta 2 /hr (latency ~30 min), zombies walk 1 ft/s (mu 0.0914 /hr per edge for 3 km cells). Humans do not move.

movie.label: Movie zombies (alpha 0.8), one random patient zero, flights

notes.calibration: walk and contact multiply the walking rate and the in-cell meeting rate (beta and kappa together, alpha unchanged) so that the 0.25-degree grid reproduces the spread of the same engine on a 3 km grid of the north-eastern US (day when the 0.25-degree square around a city loses half its people: Allentown 11 vs 12, Philadelphia 12 vs 11, Hartford 15 vs 16, Boston 27 vs 29.5, Baltimore 24 vs 25, Washington 29 vs 29). See episodes/zombie-earth/DESIGN.md.
notes.flights: Author assumption: each airline on a direct OpenFlights route = one 180-seat flight a day (about 12M seats a day, ~4.4B a year; IATA 2019: 4.5B passengers). A bitten person in an airport cell boards at rate seats/hour divided by the cell population and arrives as a zombie. After 10,000 people have been bitten worldwide, flights run at 10%.
notes.not_modelled: Cars, ships, tunnels; people running away; zombies swimming.

method: Each run is one world: one random person on Earth (weighted by population) turns; SZR with latency on a 0.25-degree grid, walking between land cells and air travel of bitten people; 90 days. A world 'took off' if at least 1,000 people were bitten. Country statistics are over worlds that took off.

inputs.population: GHS-POP R2023A, epoch 2025, 30 arc-seconds, aggregated to 0.25 degrees
